title: AWS IAM Security Audit & Least-Privilege Policy Design
description: Students audit IAM configuration in an AWS account using the AWS CLI and Prowler, identify over-permissive policies and credential hygiene issues, then design and implement least-privilege IAM policies for a sample application workload.
objective: Students will generate and interpret an IAM credential report, identify risky IAM configurations using Prowler, design a least-privilege IAM policy for a sample workload, and document findings in a cloud IAM security assessment.

steps.title: IAM Credential Report Analysis
steps.instructions:
Generate and analyse the IAM credential report to identify hygiene issues across all IAM users.

```bash
# Generate the credential report
aws iam generate-credential-report

# Wait a moment, then download and decode it
aws iam get-credential-report \
  --query 'Content' \
  --output text | base64 -d > credential_report.csv

# View with column alignment
column -t -s ',' credential_report.csv | less -S
```

**Analyse and document:**

```bash
# Users with passwords older than 90 days
awk -F',' '$6 != "N/A" && $6 != "not_supported"' credential_report.csv

# Users with MFA not enabled (column 8 = mfa_active)
grep ',false,' credential_report.csv | cut -d',' -f1

# Users with access keys not rotated in 90+ days
awk -F',' '$11 != "N/A" && $11 < "2024-01-01"' credential_report.csv
```

Create a findings table:
| Username | MFA Enabled | Password Age (days) | Last Used | Key Rotation Issue? |

steps.title: Prowler IAM Security Checks
steps.instructions:
Run Prowler's IAM-specific checks to discover misconfigurations automatically.

```bash
# Install Prowler
pip install prowler

# Run all IAM checks
prowler aws --service iam --output-formats json,html

# Run specific high-priority checks
prowler aws \
  --checks iam_root_access_key_exists \
         iam_root_mfa_enabled \
         iam_password_policy_minimum_length_14 \
         iam_support_role_created \
         iam_no_policies_attached_directly_to_users
```

**Document each finding:**
- Check ID and description
- Severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Affected resource(s)
- Prowler's remediation recommendation

**Key checks to investigate:**
- `iam_root_access_key_exists` — root should never have access keys
- `iam_password_policy_*` — password complexity requirements
- `iam_no_policies_attached_directly_to_users` — use groups/roles, not direct attachments
- `iam_user_accesskey_unused` — keys not used in 90 days should be deleted

steps.title: Identify Over-Permissive Policies
steps.instructions:
Use AWS CLI to find and analyse IAM policies with dangerous permissions.

```bash
# List all customer-managed policies
aws iam list-policies --scope Local --query 'Policies[*].[PolicyName,Arn,AttachmentCount]' --output table

# Get the full policy document for each policy
aws iam get-policy-version \
  --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:policy/POLICY_NAME \
  --version-id v1

# Find policies with wildcards (dangerous)
aws iam list-policies --scope Local | \
  jq '.Policies[] | select(.AttachmentCount > 0) | .Arn' | \
  xargs -I{} aws iam get-policy-version \
    --policy-arn {} \
    --version-id v1 \
    --query 'PolicyVersion.Document'

# Simulate what a role can do (replace with your role ARN)
aws iam simulate-principal-policy \
  --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/ROLE_NAME \
  --action-names s3:DeleteBucket iam:CreateUser ec2:TerminateInstances
```

Document: any policy containing `Action: *` or `Resource: *`, and list which principals have admin-equivalent access.

steps.title: Design & Implement a Least-Privilege Policy
steps.instructions:
Design an IAM policy for a sample web application that needs: read from S3 bucket `app-data`, write logs to CloudWatch, and read secrets from Secrets Manager.

```json
// Save as app-least-privilege-policy.json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadAppDataBucket",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::app-data",
        "arn:aws:s3:::app-data/*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Sid": "WriteCloudWatchLogs",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "logs:CreateLogStream",
        "logs:PutLogEvents"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:eu-west-1:ACCOUNT_ID:log-group:/app/production:*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "ReadAppSecret",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:eu-west-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:app/prod/db-*"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
# Create the policy
aws iam create-policy \
  --policy-name AppLeastPrivilegePolicy \
  --policy-document file://app-least-privilege-policy.json

# Create a role with this policy
aws iam create-role \
  --role-name AppProductionRole \
  --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}'

aws iam attach-role-policy \
  --role-name AppProductionRole \
  --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:policy/AppLeastPrivilegePolicy
```

Verify with simulate-principal-policy that the role CAN read S3 but CANNOT perform `s3:DeleteBucket` or `iam:CreateUser`.

steps.title: IAM Assessment Report & Remediation Plan
steps.instructions:
Compile all findings into a structured IAM security assessment.

**Run Prowler one final time and export the HTML report:**
```bash
prowler aws --service iam --output-formats html
# Open prowler_output/html/prowler_output.html
```

**Build your assessment report with these sections:**

```
1. Credential Hygiene Summary
   Table: Username | MFA | Key Age | Key Last Used | Risk

2. IAM Policy Findings
   Table: Policy Name | Issue | Severity | Affected Principals

3. Prowler Findings Summary
   Table: Check ID | Description | Severity | Status | Remediation

4. Implemented Control: Least-Privilege Policy
   - Policy JSON
   - Simulate-policy output (PASS/FAIL for each action tested)

5. Remediation Roadmap
   Priority 1 (immediate):
   - Delete root access keys
   - Enable MFA for all users with console access
   - Rotate access keys older than 90 days
   
   Priority 2 (this week):
   - Move user policies to groups
   - Replace wildcard policies with least-privilege equivalents
   - Enable CloudTrail in all regions
```

Screenshot the Prowler HTML report summary page and include it in the submission.

expected_output: An IAM Security Assessment report (PDF) covering: credential report analysis table, Prowler findings (minimum 5 documented), over-permissive policy identification with evidence, least-privilege policy JSON and simulate-policy verification output, and a prioritised remediation roadmap.
